narrow: The current implication assumes only that the refinement class is a singleton. If its unique refinement is incompatible with \(p\), then its canonical feasible set is empty, ordinary minimum and maximum are undefined, and the nonempty-fiber theorem cannot be invoked. Adding nonemptiness of the summary fiber is the minimal domain restriction; it makes the unique canonical program feasible without changing either conclusion on the theorem's intended domain.
